chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Ukeyl al-Nuymari, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who rented a house and therein was a garden, so he cultivated in the garden and planted palm trees, and trees, and fruits, and other than that, and did not consult the owner of the garden regarding that. So he (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is the rent, and the owner of the house would evaluate the planting and the cultivation for a fair price, so he would give it to the planter; and if he had consulted, so upon him is the rent, and for him is the planting and the cultivation. He could have uprooted it and gone with it wherever he so desired.
ai.seo_question: What are the rights and obligations of a tenant who plants trees in a rented garden without the owner's prior consent?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'gharsh' (planting) in tenancy, distinguishing between unauthorized and permitted cultivation to balance the landlord's right to the land with the tenant's investment. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness (adl), ensuring the tenant is compensated for improvements if the owner claims them, while allowing the tenant to remove them if consent was given. This ruling underscores the contractual nature of tenancy in Islamic law, where ownership of movable improvements remains distinct from the immovable land.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Musa Bin Akeyl Al Numeyri, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding

a man who rented a house and therein was a garden, so he cultivated in the garden and planted palm trees, and (other) trees, and fruits (trees), and other than that, and the owner of the garden had not instructed him so. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is the rent, and the owner of the house would evaluate the plants, and the cultivation for a fair price, so he would give it to the planter; and if it was that he had instructed it, so upon him would be the rent, and for him would be the plants and the cultivation. He could have uprooted it and gone with it wherever he so desired to’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from Musa ibn ‘Ukayl al-Numayriy from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “About

the case of a man who rents a house in which there is a garden, in the garden he plants palm trees and other fruit bearing trees and fruits and so on without permission from the owner of the garden. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must pay the rent and the owner of the garden evaluates the plantation in a fair manner and pays to the man who had planted them. Had he asked permission he had to pay the rent and the plantation belonged to him, which he had to cut off and take whenever he wanted.’”
